Q: How can I check out a GitHub pull request with Git? A:

The problem with some of options above, is that if someone pushes more commits to the pull request after opening the pull request, they won't give you the most updated version.

For me what worked best was: Go to the pull request, and press 'Commits', scroll to the bottom to see the most recent commit hash value:

And then simply use Git checkout, i.e.,

git checkout <commit number>

In the above example

git checkout 0ba1a50

Q: Problems linking boost with cmake: undefined reference to boost::program_options A:

You are using old CMake code patterns. You should not use include_directories anymore. Use modern CMake and let target_link_libraries with proper arguments of targets do this job (it will link library and setup includes at the same time).

cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.10.0)
project(test_opencv VERSION 0.1.0 LANGUAGES C CXX)

find_package(OpenCV REQUIRED)
message(STATUS " OpenCV Version: ${OpenCV_VERSION}")

find_package(Boost 1.4.0 COMPONENTS program_options REQUIRED)
message(STATUS " Boost Version: ${Boost_VERSION}")

add_executable(test_opencv main.cpp)

# apparently OpenCV do not provide nice cmake alias like other libraries
# target_link_libraries(test_opencv PUBLIC OpenCV::OpenCV)
# so here is working version:
target_include_directories(test_opencv PUBLIC ${Boost_INCLUDE_DIRS})
target_link_libraries(test_opencv PUBLIC ${OpenCV_LIBS})

# this one I'm using and it works.
target_link_libraries(test_opencv PUBLIC Boost::program_options)

Tested it works on my machine.

Q: How to correctly define next/font in Next.js Pages Router with Tailwind v4's in-css configuration? A:

one hour later ...

The variables will NOT get defined - I have not found a way around it. However, I did find two solutions to apply my desired font that give an identical result.

Solution 1 - tailwind native

When importing the fonts, add the class for the "default" variant, here font-sans

<div id="App" className={`${inter.variable} ${interTight.variable} ${robotoMono.variable} font-sans flex ...

Solution 2 - next/font native

Include the "default" font additionally via its .className accessor

<div id="App" className={`${inter.className} ${inter.variable} ${interTight.variable} ${robotoMono.variable} flex ...

Q: Disable add, edit and delete views and widgets for a custom Wagtail ViewSet index page A:

If you don't want CRUD, why use a ViewSet. I suggest you create the Index View and add a link to it from where ever you want to show it. (With both settings and admin menu set to False, it isn't clear to me where that is.) The docs cover this in detail https://docs.wagtail.org/en/stable/extending/admin_views.html But I would probably start by subclassing the generic IndexView which is the only part of the ModelViewSet you want to retain. I think that's this code but check to make sure there isn't a better starting point for your use case: https://github.com/wagtail/wagtail/blob/40c9b1fdff19bad5b9997c0366ed5cb642edd557/wagtail/admin/views/generic/models.py#L68
